text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing tiny negative invoice balances after lease revocations on Dedicated GPU pools. spotted on EU region, tenant T-443 and T-991. 
maya: ugh. negative microbalances like -0.0002 tokens?
alex: yep. looks like a short window after revocation where streaming meter records one last chunk then a cleanup credit arrives. sequence: lease revoke -> routing fallback -> duplicate end-event.
liam: can you paste the raw event payload?
alex: here, scrubbed ids:
```
{
  "tenant":"T-443",
  "event":"session_end",
  "tokens": 124,
  "routing":"dedicated-eu-42",
  "lease_revoked": true,
  "timestamp": 1746004319
}
```
maya: billing-bot shows an adjustment right after?
billing-bot: Generated adjustment ADJ-9821 for T-443 (-0.0002) at 1746004325, status: pending.
elena: maybe dedupe window on the event ingestion is too narrow for revoke+fallback path. we have a 500ms dedupe TTL in ingest-sidecar.
sree: timeline theory: request hits dedicated node, lease revoke triggered mid-stream, proxy re-routes to fallback hosted, hosted emits end-event, dedicated emits end-event later during cleanup -> double count then quick adjustment.
liam: interesting. do we see this only for short sessions / streaming?
alex: mainly streaming with early revoke. courtsey example where client cancels mid-response.
ops-bot: link to logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/streams/T-443/1746004310-1746004350
maya: quick check: how many tenants affected in last 24h?
billing-bot: Scanning... 72 tenants with micro-adjustments (<0.01 tokens) in EU in last 24h.
elena: 72 is small but annoying — causes invoice noise and reconciliation churn with finance.
sree: fix options: 1) widen ingest dedupe window to 2s (risk: suppress legit duplicate retries) 2) add lease-revoke marker that makes end-events idempotent 3) move adjustment generation to post-aggregation pass rather than immediately on ingest.
liam: I'd prefer #2 (idempotent marker) first — minimal blast radius. we can use existing request_id + lease_revoked boolean to build idempotency key.
maya: timeline on #2?
liam: prototype in 1 day, can canary in EU next week.
elena: ops: will this change affect billing latency?
liam: negligible. it's just dedupe on the ingest pipeline before enqueue to aggregator.
alex: also can we surface a small flag in Console billing UI to collapse micro-adjustments (<0.01 tokens) into a single line item? reduces noise for customers.
maya: yes, UX can show "micro-adjustments collapsed" with a tooltip. I can mock.
sree: long-term, we should also add a metric: count_adjustments_by_reason so we can alert on spikes.
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-1453 (dedupe-by-lease marker) assigned to @liam.
liam: I'll open PR against ingest-sidecar and add unit tests for idempotency key.
elena: finance FYI @finance-team — we might still see historical ones until backfill runs.
alex: thanks team. will post canary results here once PR is live. :thumbsup:
